thread:
alex.c: Quick async check on the pricing change work — two small but important dependency questions for metering/billing before we freeze the schema today.
julia.n: got it. outline the items and owners? I can take the metering mapping one if needed.
alex.c: thanks. Items: 1) quota overrides for contracted enterprise customers (how/where to apply in metering pipeline), 2) billing adapter id mapping for legacy plans, 3) edge-case for negative usage adjustments from refunds. Owners: unclear.
pranav.s: I can own quota overrides. Need to know if contracts should override per-route or per-customer globally. Prefer per-customer at ingestion so we can short-circuit batching.
kevin_r: @pranav.s per-route would let us keep SLOs tighter for paid routes. If we do per-customer at ingestion, we risk leaking quota to other routes. What's the contract model? @julia.n can you confirm contract granularity?
julia.n: Contracts are usually at customer-account level, but there are addenda that scope to product-line (e.g., embeddings-only). We should support both. My preference: store a contract flag at customer scope + optional route_allowlist.
samir: +1 to route_allowlist. For implementation: metering pipeline currently applies quota using customer_id and route_id downstream. If contract is account-scoped, we can add a contract_effective_routes array at ingestion and expand to per-route rows.
alex.c: sounds reasonable. Pranav: can you capture the ingestion change in a small PR? Something like adding a contract_routes expansion step.
pranav.s: yes. I'll prototype a delta in the metering repo. quick sketch:
```py
# on ingest
contract = fetch_contract(customer_id)
if contract:
    routes = contract.get('routes') or all_routes_for_account()
    for r in routes:
        emit_usage_row(customer_id, r, usage)
else:
    emit_usage_row(customer_id, route_id, usage)
```
I'll open a draft PR by EOD.
kevin_r: nice. Second item: billing adapter id mapping for legacy plans. We have old plan_ids that billing expects; pricing change will introduce new rate_card_ids. We need a stable mapping table or transform layer.
julia.n: billing team asked that we keep a compatibility layer for at least one billing cycle. I can coordinate with them. Do we need this in metering or in billing-adapter service?
samir: easier to handle in billing-adapter service — keep metering emitting canonical rate_card_id, adapter maps old_plan_id -> rate_card_id for legacy invoices. But if the issuer of usage still tags old_plan_id, metering needs to normalize.
alex.c: tradeoffs: adapter mapping centralizes legacy logic (cleaner), but if metering normalizes earlier we avoid downstream surprises. I'd push a small normalization step in metering that emits both canonical_rate_card_id and original_plan_id.
pranav.s: agree. I'll add fields: canonical_rate_card_id and legacy_plan_id. Adapter can ignore legacy if not needed.
metering-bot: CI status: metering/ingest-tests — flaky on contract-expansion test (2 failures).
pranav.s: noted, will fix tests in draft PR.
alex.c: last item: negative usage adjustments (refunds). Billing needs a signed adjustment that can be applied idempotently. How do you all want those represented in the pipeline? negative rows, or separate adjustment objects?
julia.n: billing prefers adjustment records that reference original invoice ids, but metering currently just emits negative usage rows. We should add an adjustment envelope:
```
{ "type": "adjustment", "original_invoice": "inv_123", "amount_tokens": -12345, "reason": "refund" }
```
This keeps semantics clear.
samir: implementable. We'll add a new message_type on the Kafka topic: usage | adjustment. Billing-adapter will treat adjustments specially and require invoice_ref.
kevin_r: timeline check: can we have draft PRs + adapter stub by tomorrow EOD so legal can review contract override behavior on Friday? We need to ship schema freeze next week.
pranav.s: draft PR for ingestion + tests by EOD today. Will add contract expansion and canonical_rate_card fields.
julia.n: I'll sync with billing for adapter mapping and confirm legal questions. Happy to join any short call.
alex.c: awesome. @kevin_r please tag finance/legal when adapter mapping plan is ready. I'll add these three items to the rollout checklist and mark dependencies. Thanks all :thumbsup:
